title: I have been having a ton of fun developing games with Opus 5. Does anyone feel it's even better than Fable/GPT-5.6?
author: cody-fifth-door
selftext:
It's pretty incredible how much of a leap it is for 3D visuals. I made a ps1 style liminal driving game and it just... nailed it. Seriously, all these game ideas I have had for years being doable by just a single prompt is a bit overwhelming!   
  
I'm really feeling the singularity these days.

comments.author: victorrseloy2
comments.body: For my day-to-day job as a backend software engineer, I prefer Fable and GPT-5.6. For game dev, though, Opus 5 is an absolute beast.

replies.author: cody-fifth-door
replies.body: This is where I am at basically. Fable is still great but Opus 5 has a sort of je ne sais quoi especially when you just let it cook for a few hours.

comments.author: Wikkid_witch
comments.body: Are you using a game engine or just prompting from scratch

comments.author: liright
comments.body: It's better than 5.6 but it's not even close to being as good as Fable. Fable is a whole another level.

replies.author: Silver-Chipmunk7744
replies.body:
I think it depends on what you want to do.

if you plug it on a gauntlet loop and ask it to look like some AAA game, i think Opus beats Fable. Opus does really good looking outputs.

5.6 shines when it's more of a backend issue... Say your NPC keeps getting lost, 5.6 is great at debugging.

But i think Fable shines when your goal involves a combination of complexity AND taste. For example "can you actually make my large waves look good?".

replies.author: wllmsaccnt
replies.body:
Fable is slower, but more token efficient, so it tends to get output heavy tasks done faster and with context size overhead. I also MUCH prefer its explanations. 

Opus 5 uses technical and concise language, which sounds great until you realize that means you have to memorize every planning section header and requirement symbol. Every summary is "P4 gated on D5 failed to pass and was deferred to P7 for the smoke test".

comments.body: This is good information. I have been wondering where to put funding toward. I tried Seele and it doesn't seem to ever work out. I've output one project but the others constantly ask for money for credits and I don't know that I want to push it further to get to the final output.

comments.author: DocHolidayPhD
comments.body: Even today, if you think a single prompt is pushing out high quality games, you're overlooking a lot.

comments.author: ScutFarkush
comments.body: i can never tell if fable is good because it eats all of my credits on the max plan in 2 heavy prompts. open 5 is a sweet spot and has been much getter for my game than 4.8 is, but i am consistently hitting my 5 hour limits around the 4 hour mark now, but i get a lot of quality work done.
